objective: Run the MATLAB-derived double-pendulum swing-up and LQR capture on the existing C++ hardware path after entering balance auto.
known: The cart, encoders, voltage output, homing, limit debounce and double LQR already exist in PendulumLab.
The first absolute encoder is 8000 counts/revolution and the second relative encoder is 4000 counts/revolution.
Both encoder count directions and the absolute theta2 conversion were previously verified.
The control path runs at 200 Hz and converts acceleration to a velocity reference and then to AO voltage.
implemented: Added the MATLAB-derived three-stage supervisor to DoublePendulumLqrController.
Added deterministic kick-off from an exactly stationary downward state.
Added automatic stationary downward-zero capture for both encoders.
Relaxed downward-zero capture to a sliding 1.5 s window with configurable 3.6 degree peak-to-peak tolerance for each link and a 30 s timeout.
Added balance auto and balance start command selection to the double-balance executable.
Added a non-terminating +/-0.30 m software boundary that replaces outward commands with a configurable 0.03 V inward recovery command and then resumes swing-up.
Made automatic mode persistent: a stage-3 fall returns to stage 1 or 2 based on which link left the recovery envelope, and later capture attempts continue without restarting the process.
Superseded the interim hardware-log-based tuning because the operator reported manual assistance in those runs; those logs are not used as optimization evidence.

A deterministic nonlinear model-only robustness search selected 2.00x paper-adapted stage-1 gains, a 0.12 m/s stage-1 speed gate, stage-2 far/near gains 1.40/5.00, a 9 rad/s capture-assist eligibility limit, and a 0.005 J second-link energy target; the 1 V hardware output ceiling is unchanged.
Kept physical limit debounce, encoder jump checks, sample timeout, software travel stop, AO saturation and safe shutdown.
Added stage and capture-time telemetry while preserving immutable per-run directories.
validation: Software-boundary tests passed for left/right outward blocking, inward pass-through, and reversed motor polarity.
The relaxed sliding-window downward-zero build passed the full CTest regression and configuration validation.
The selected friction-allowance gains retained a successful 1-2-3 capture in a 60 s nonlinear MATLAB regression, with maximum simulated cart travel 0.117 m for the tested combination.
C++ unit tests passed for stage-3 first-link fall to stage 1 and second-link fall to stage 2, followed by a successful release build and --validate-only check.
Earlier hardware-log observations are retained only as run history and were excluded from final parameter selection because manual assistance contaminated the trajectories.

At the MATLAB/Simulink 1 ms step, the selected model-only parameters completed and settled all 18 full 100 s nonlinear scenarios spanning six symmetric downward initial states and three actuator/friction profiles, with no 0.35 m hard-stop failure, mean capture time 41.200 s, and worst cart travel 0.3081 m.

At the real controller's 5 ms sample period, the same parameters completed 16 of 18 full scenarios and 16 of 18 isolated stage-2 scenarios without a hard-limit failure; the two full misses were the exactly symmetric ideal downward starts, while perturbed starts completed.

The final generated Simulink model completed stages 1-2-3 from a small asymmetric downward perturbation, captured at 45.965 s, settled by 50 s, used 0.1279 m maximum cart travel, and passed run_simulation validation.
The 1.50x comparison completed 16 of 18 scenarios and reached the 0.35 m hard limit twice, so it was rejected.
The updated configuration parsed successfully and the full C++ CTest suite passed while the active hardware run was left untouched.
The double-balance configuration passed --validate-only in automatic mode.
After the model-only parameter update, the Release build, complete CTest suite, and --validate-only configuration check all passed again.
No actuator-output test was run by Codex.
next_authorized_step: A supervised physical run initiated by the user with balance auto.
promotion_rule: Three consecutive successful hardware captures with no safety trip before promotion to known-good.
